title: evaluation question batch output (NNN.out.json) and the merged row
description: Two contracts in one file because they are one shape at two moments. `#` (the top level) is what `question-forger` writes next to its `.in.json`: an envelope plus `questions[]`, each of which must be derivable from ONE path in that input. `#/$defs/row` is what `brain eval questions merge` appends to data/eval/questions.jsonl — the same fields plus the bookkeeping the merge adds (`origin`, `batch_id`, `shape`) and one relaxation: a competency question carried over from Plan 2 has no gold yet, so `gold_source` may be `pending` and `gold_answer` may be null. Four rules merge enforces that a schema cannot state: every `source_path_id` must be a path in the matching `.in.json`; every `gold_evidence` entry must exist in the graph (or, when prefixed `truth:`, in data/canonical/synthetic_truth.json); a key on the ANSWER side of the path must not appear verbatim in the question (leakage); and the accepted set must hit the per-type/per-language plan the build wrote into MANIFEST.json.

batch_id.description: Exactly the `batch_id` of the .in.json this answers, e.g. "shard-01/002".

questions.description: One entry per `asks[]` slot in the input, in any order. A path you cannot write a fair question about is a `failed` entry in status.json (or a substitution from a `spare: true` path of the same type), never a silently missing question.

notes.description: Free-text remarks for the planner — a path whose snippets contradict its edges, a shape that produced only unfair questions. Never a place to hide a rule you could not follow.

type.description: The question type (spec §5.1). Copied from the path's `question_type`; a question of a different type than the path it came from unbalances the set.

lang.description: The language the question is written in. Identifiers (KAFKA-…, KIP-…, XT-…, component names, versions) stay untranslated in both.

gold_source.description: Where the gold answer comes from, which is what makes the leakage guard meaningful. `graph` = a fact the extracted graph states; `text` = a fact the raw chunk text states, so S1 can reach it without the graph; `truth` = data/canonical/synthetic_truth.json, the known truth of the synthetic Xray/ADO layer. `pending` is reserved for the merge, for a competency question whose gold the planner still owes.

strategy.description: The strategy you would expect to win this question (spec §4): s1 hybrid, s2 graph-enhanced vector, s3 entity-anchored local, s4 guarded Text2Cypher, s5 global community search, s6 temporal tools. A hint for the run matrix, never a restriction on it — mode A runs every strategy on every question anyway.

evidence_id.description: One citable key from the path: a node key exactly as the input spells it (`KAFKA-14649`, `KIP-848`, `XT-10007`, a 40-hex commit sha, `Decision|…`, `L0-6`), a chunk id from `snippets[].chunk_id`, or `truth:<section>:<index>` for a synthetic-truth excerpt offered in `truth[]`. Never a key you did not see in this batch.

id.description: `q` + three digits, unique across the whole set, e.g. "q007". The build reserves a disjoint id range per shard in the input's `id_range`; use ids from it so two shards never collide.

question.description: What a real engineer would type. It may name the path's `anchors[]`; it must NOT contain any key listed in the path's `answers[]`, and must not restate the gold answer — merge rejects both.

gold_answer.description: The correct answer in one or two sentences, in the SAME language as the question, naming the keys a right answer must contain. Derivable from this path alone.

gold_evidence.description: Every key or chunk id a correct answer has to rest on — this is what layer 2 measures recall against, so a key that is merely related does not belong here.

difficulty.description: 1 = one hop from the anchor, 2 = two hops or a join, 3 = three or more hops, an aggregation, or a whole-corpus theme.

source_path_id.description: The `path_id` of the path in this batch the question came from, copied exactly.

notes.description: Optional: why this question is fair, or what about the path made it hard.

row.description: One line of data/eval/questions.jsonl. Everything `question` requires, with gold allowed to be pending for the 19 competency questions carried over from Plan 2, plus what the merge stamps.

id.description: `q###` for a forged question, `cq##` for a competency question.

origin.description: `forged` = written by question-forger from a sampled path; `competency` = one of the 19 questions brain competency built from the graph in Plan 2.

difficulty_source.description: `forged` = the agent judged it from the path; `type_default` = the merge filled the type's default because a competency question has no path to count hops on.

gold_derived_by.description: Who produced the gold. `agent` = question-forger wrote it from the path; `code` = `brain eval questions gold-competency` derived it from the graph with a fixed query; `planner` = a human wrote it.

gold_query.description: With `gold_derived_by: code`: the Cypher, or the name and arguments of the deterministic retrieval function, that produced this answer. It is what makes the gold auditable — re-run it and you must get the same facts.

gold_note.description: Why a row is still `pending`: what the derivation looked for and what came back. Never an excuse for an answer that was not derived.

shape.description: The path shape the question came from (`brain/eval/paths.py`), or null for a competency question.

batch_id.description: The batch the question arrived in, or null for a competency question.

pair.description: Competency only: the tag that ties an English row to its Hebrew twin for the cross-lingual comparison.

anchors.description: The keys the question is allowed to name — its subject, not its answer.
